body: If this file asserts something doesn't exist, grep the implementing directory across the full tree first. Existence claims need existence-disproving evidence.
Before this commit message claims fixed/covers/handles X: confirm the staged diff contains the file:line implementing X. If not, drop the claim.
Every non-trivial verdict in this audit needs a file:line or this-session runtime evidence pointer, added at write time. Verify uncited rows before sending.
Check whether anything was deferred earlier. A terse continuation does not lift a deferral — do only the unambiguous part, or ask one line.
When you mention this file to the user, make the first mention an absolute path starting with / or ~, not a bare filename.
Name the current caller for every new exported function/type here. No caller, or an existing primitive already fits? Don't create it.
Write source markdown, never renderer output. Scan the first ~20 lines: uniform 2-space indent or '…' inside table rows means rendered-output-saved-as-source — rewrite it.
For any comment over 3 lines: name the single load-bearing fact, write only that in 1-2 lines. Still longer? It's an essay — move it to a doc and link.
Before renaming: run `rg -F '<old-name>'` across the whole repo and fix every hit outside the file you edit. Updating the writer is not updating the contract.
This is a cached artifact, not live state. Re-derive the claim from a live source (ps, process tree, env, sourcing the file) before asserting which session/tty/writer is real.
Persist juror/sub-agent verdicts through the data layer: use `atone add --case-file <path>` so the output lands on disk. Never relay a verdict by hand from a return string.
Before drafting design questions: name the 3-5 composite user stories this surface serves and tie each question to one. Don't emit a list of independent taste option-picks.
